subject: Marketplace publisher sandbox access, identity proofs, and technical questions
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@microsoft.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-30 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Welcome — next steps for publisher onboarding and sandbox access

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the intake form — welcome to the Azure Marketplace onboarding track. To get you into the publisher sandbox and validate the offer manifest we need the following items from your side:

1) Publisher identity proof (PDF) showing legal entity name.
2) A service principal we can use to validate the publisher manifest (we prefer a contributor-level SP with onboarding ttl).
3) The initial offer manifest (ZIP or Excel) and a list of intended SKUs.

I attached a short service-principal-setup guide and a manifest checklist that mirrors the validation gates. If you can drop the identity proof and grant a temporary SP by EOD Friday we can schedule a short validation session next week.

Quick question: are you planning co-sell registration as part of the initial publish or as a follow-up? That affects the entitlement mapping in the manifest.

Cheers,
Samir 
Marketplace Programs – Azure ISV Engagement
Microsoft Corporation

Attachment stubs: service-principal-setup-guide.pdf (doc), manifest-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@microsoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-01 07:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Welcome — next steps for publisher onboarding and sandbox access

Samir — thanks, this is helpful. A few notes and questions from our side: 

- Identity proof: attached (publisher_id_proof.pdf). This is our legal entity PDF.
- SP access: we can create a short-lived service principal in the Redmond validation subscription and give you contributor; can you confirm the tenant ID we should use?
- Manifest: Marissa is working on the SKU matrix. We expect two SKUs (standard, enterprise) and one free trial SKU.
- Co-sell: we want co-sell enabled at publish time; we will need guidance on the co-sell metadata fields and partner ID mapping.

Two technical validation questions to confirm: 
1) Are there any runtime scanning checks for custom containers that would block our image if it has an uncommon base layer? We plan to publish a containerized inference endpoint.
2) What are the service principal permissions required for automated manifest validation versus a human-led check?

Proposed next steps: you confirm tenant ID and we provide SP + manifest by Thursday. Can we book a 30 min validation slot on Friday PST?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: publisher_id_proof.pdf (pdf)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@microsoft.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-02 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Welcome — next steps for publisher onboarding and sandbox access

Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the identity doc. Tenant & SP details below and answers to your questions: 

Tenant we will use for validation: 72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47

Service principal permissions: for the automated manifest validation service we need at minimum:
- Reader on the subscription (to enumerate resources)
- Microsoft.Web/sites/* permissions for any App Service validation steps (if you deploy that way)
- AcrPull if you're using ACR images (image inspection pipeline)

If you prefer, give us contributor for the short window — that's the fastest route and we've used it for other ISVs. Please set the SP expiry to 7 days.

Container scanning: we run a metadata and vulnerability verification on container layers and base images. Uncommon base layers are allowed but may trigger a manual review which can add 24–48 hours. The main blockers are images requiring privileged host access or non-standard kernel modules.

On co-sell metadata: include the following fields in the manifest: partnerId (MS partner ID), coSellEligible (boolean), solutionType, and a brief go-to-market description. I can share a sample JSON after this mail.

I'll hold a 30-minute slot on Friday 11:00–11:30 PST for the validation. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

—Samir

Samir — Friday works, invited the team and included our Acme partner (Devon) who will own the container deployment in their tenant. Notes for the validation session: 

Action items before the call (owner):
- Create SP in tenant 72f988bf-86f1-41af-91ab-2d7cd011db47, set expiry 7 days (Vivek).
- Upload final manifest + SKU matrix to shared Drive folder (Marissa).
- Prepare container image with non-privileged runtime; include SBOM and base image info (Devon / Acme).
- Confirm co-sell partner ID and add to manifest (Karthik).

Questions to clarify on the call:
- Manual review SLA if container triggers vulnerability flags.
- How co-sell enablement impacts marketplace listing fields vs. post-publish registration.
- Any mandatory telemetry or logging headers required for azure entitlement checks.

I'll attach the manifest checklist and the SP guide to the calendar invite. See you Friday at 11.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference
